subject: Intermittent surge of 5xx/429s during peak — suspected NAT translation imbalance
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@clientfin.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s during peak traffic

Hi Irene / Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses to Redwood endpoints around 08:45 PST. Error rate climbed from ~0.4% to ~8% across a handful of customer-facing routes; tail latency also jumped. This is on our Dedicated deployment (VPC peered to our VPC).

What we observed:
- 429s correlate with client retries and continued bursts — looks like a retry amplification.
- Many 5xx responses have upstream connection timeouts to your edge (timeout / connection reset).
- NAT translation counters on our side show SNAT table exhaustion spikes at the same time.

We attached packet traces and NAT metrics. Can we get an immediate sync? This is affecting a number of our production customers and our SRE execs are on standby.

Attachments: clientfin_conn-traces-20261120.pcap, nat-metrics-20261120.csv

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
Senior SRE, ClientFin
ops@clientfin.com

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:25:41 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429s during peak traffic — initial triage notes

FYI — initial triage from infra/network on the bridge. Summary (raw):

- Timeline: ClientFin observed start ~08:45. Redwood edge metrics show a sudden increase in upstream connection resets and short TCP connect timeouts to our Dedicated egress in us-west-2.
- Hypothesis: transient SNAT translation exhaustion on ClientFin-side NAT combined with client retry policies caused a retry storm; at the same time we observed a small spike in connection churn on our side (conn-tracking entries climbing) likely due to TCP sockets in TIME_WAIT piling up from short-lived client retries.
- Supporting data: attached nat-metrics-20261120.csv (SNAT overviews), and a pcap showing many SYN retries followed by RSTs.

Immediate mitigation recommendations (ordered):
1) Ask ClientFin to temporarily increase SNAT ephemeral port pool and connection tracking limits.
2) On Redwood side, open a secondary egress path for the peered VPC (route to alternate NAT gateway or permit egress via a different AZ) to reduce single-point SNAT contention.
3) Apply short-term rate-limiting on repeat clients traffic at the edge (throttle high-RPS IPs) to break amplification loops.
4) Enable connection reuse and longer keepalive on intermediate proxies where safe to reduce ephemeral churn.

We’ve created a ticket (INF-9873) and dropped an initial incident timeline PDF into the drive. I’m assigning infra engineers to work this; Marcus Lin will try a quick health-check on firewall conntrack thresholds and latency on the peering link.

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:02:11 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s during peak traffic — Redwood status and next steps

Carlos —

Thank you for the traces and patience. Quick update from Redwood exec/SRE side after the 09:30 bridge: we agree this is an elevated incident caused by a combination of client-side SNAT exhaustion and retry amplification leading to transient overload on the Dedicated peering path.

What we’ve done so far:
- Deployed temporary edge-level client-rate limiting rules for the affected IP ranges to mitigate the retry storm.
- Provisioned a backup egress path for the ClientFin peering (multi-AZ NAT failover).
- Pulled an emergency config change to increase conntrack table size on the Dedicated egress nodes to handle short-lived bursts; monitoring metrics now show steady decline in TIME_WAIT growth.

Next steps (timeline):
- 10:30 PST: Confirm stability for next 1h; keep rate-limits in place.
- Today EOD: Follow up with permanent recommendations (SNAT sizing, retry backoff guidance, and a hardened peering runbook).
- We will produce a post-incident doc and timeline (INF-9873) and share with your SRE/exec team by COB.

We are available for an executive sync if you’d like — suggested time 10:30 PST. Please let us know.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your customers and appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
